text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple Route53 healthcheck failures and missing probe telemetry for eu-west-2 AZ-B. checks: hb/service-*/tcp-heartbeat. triggered: PD-INC-9712. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/healthchecks/euw2?panel=probe-telemetry

Alex R: acked the PD. Jamie (on-call) you up? I can start triage but need someone to lead mitigation.

Jamie (on-call): On call, taking lead. first pass: are failures real or a telemetry gap? can someone run a direct curl from our external probe hosts to the backend and paste results?

Lee N: I'm seeing probe hosts in euw2 failing to resolve internal DNS names intermittently. dig +short svc.internal.example returns nothing ~30% of the time from two probes. Might be a transient VPC resolver issue or a new firewall rule.

Maria S: pulling probe logs now. doing tail -n 200 on probe containers.

Maria S (code): ```
# tail -n 200 /var/log/healthprobe/probe-euw2-azb.log | grep -E "ERROR|MISSING|TIMEOUT"
2025-09-03T09:12:01Z ERROR check=heartbeat instance=ld-201 timeout=15000ms connect=timeout
2025-09-03T09:12:03Z WARN  check=heartbeat instance=ld-202 dns_lookup=failed
2025-09-03T09:12:07Z ERROR check=heartbeat instance=ld-203 tcp_connect=refused
```

Maria S: logs show DNS lookup failures and TCP connect refused. not just alert flapping. also notice a gap in probe telemetry between 09:11:30 and 09:12:00 (metrics missing).

Jamie (on-call): ok. customer visible impact? any uptick in 5xx from eu-west-2?

Alex R: quick SLO check: small bump in 5xx starting 09:11 UTC, error budget burn ~0.3% in last 15m for eu-west-2 app endpoints. some customers seeing transient errors. not a full region outage.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-9712 escalated to level1.

eng-infra-bot: Recommended runbook: network-probe-loss -> step 1: check probe host networking and firewall ACLs.

Lee N: I'm checking recent infra changes. There's a scheduled maintenance change earlier that applied a tightened SG on a subset of probe hosts in eu-west-2 to block ephemeral source ports. change-id: CHG-33211 applied ~08:58 UTC. Could be related.

Jamie (on-call): if that's true we could be seeing probes being blocked by a security group rule. Lee, can you revert or open ports temporarily? keep change window notes.

Lee N: reverting now to previous SG policy for the affected probe hosts. applying rollback patch.

Lee N (code): ```bash
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules --group-id sg-0abcd --region eu-west-2 --revoke-rules '[{"IpProtocol":"tcp","FromPort":1024,"ToPort":65535,"CidrIpv4":"0.0.0.0/0"}]'
# rolling back to allow ephemeral source ports for probe hosts
```

Maria S: after SG rollback, probes started reporting again. telemetry gap closed at 09:15. healthcheck failures dropping. evidence points to SG change causing packet drops and DNS failures.

Alex R: good find. Jamie, propose we silence Route53 healthcheck alerts for 20m while we validate and avoid unnecessary pages. we should still monitor metrics and not auto-close issues.

Jamie (on-call): agreed. /silence alert:route53-healthchecks:euw2-azb duration=20m reason=rollback-in-flight

Maria S: capturing reproduction steps and making RDW ticket: RDW-5582 "euw2 probe telemetry loss caused by SG CHG-33211". adding logs, diff of SG rules, timeline. recommending: revert CHG-33211 in all regions where probes use ephemeral ports; add preflight checks for probe IP ranges in change-runbooks.

Lee N: doing a quick connectivity smoke test: dig +short svc.internal.example @10.0.0.2 (VPC resolver) -> now returns correctly. curl from probe host to app endpoint returns 200.

Alex R: customer comms draft for #customer-status: "We experienced elevated healthcheck failures in eu-west-2 AZ-B due to a misapplied security group change impacting probe telemetry. We rolled back the change and are monitoring; some customers may have seen transient errors between 09:11-09:16 UTC." I'll post after Jamie signs off.

Jamie (on-call): post the blurb. also plan followup: 1) permanent rollback of the SG patch to remove the restrictive rule for probe IPs; 2) add an automated pre-deploy check to block changes that would affect probe ephemeral ports; 3) retro with infra ops to tighten change validation. assign owners: Maria -> rollback verification & RDW-5582, Lee -> infra change fix & preflight, Alex -> customer comms & postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-9712 acknowledged by Alex R. next escalation in 15m.

Maria S: verifying metrics: 5xx rates back to baseline, probe error rate <0.2% in last 10m. capturing final logs and attaching to ticket.

eng-infra-bot: runbook update logged by Jamie: network-probe-loss -> step "revert SG" completed. awaiting postmortem creation.

Lee N: creating CHG rollback record and adding the preflight check to the change template. also marking CHG-33211 as emergency rollback.

Alex R: posted customer-status update. monitoring for 30m and then we'll unsilence. good work team.

Jamie (on-call): final check before we close: any residual DNS or TCP errors in eu-west-2 in last 5m?

Maria S: last 5m shows no failures, telemetry stable.

Lee N: edge and NLB metrics normal.

Alex R: handing to postmortem queue. incident mode -> mitigated; followups -> RDW-5582 (change validation, preflight), CHG-33211 rollback audit. owners pinned as above. closing thread in 20m if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
